item.text: The key distinction is that home medications and allergies are repeated snapshots, while lab entries are copies of individual results. I’ll prefer a stay’s discharge medication list, preserve “held” even when restarting is discouraged, and use accession plus test code to deduplicate labs.

I’ll use local dates and recorded times for the as-of cutoff, then apply supersession and retraction before mapping any rows. For conditions, I’ll keep confirmed history, exclude unconfirmed working diagnoses, and avoid letting copied medical history overwrite a clinician’s newer CKD assessment.

Lab mapping now selects the most advanced copy before parsing its value, so an unreportable corrected result cannot revive an older numeric value. Next I’m handling drug-attributed diagnoses as allergy/intolerance rows, including resolving a named class to a drug only when that same document lists exactly one match.
